fields.justification: Stable identity is required for evidence and cross-reference integrity.
Classification makes completeness and policy checks deterministic.
The accepted or disputed meaning must remain explicit.
Required versus optional meaning controls terminal status.
Proposed, accepted, unresolved, disputed, unsupported, refused, and invalid meaning cannot be conflated.
Every accepted claim needs visible authority.
No requirement may exist without attributable source evidence.
A requirement must expose how its meaning will be proven.
Consequential meaning invokes approval and fail-closed rules.
Approval evidence is conditional on consequential meaning.
Default-derived meaning must identify the visible authorized default.
Stable source identity prevents silent evidence substitution.
Producer surfaces remain attributable while converging on one contract.
Byte-backed sources require content identity; ephemeral claims may lack bytes.
Current, missing, replaced, and withdrawn evidence have different validity.
A source assertion is evidence, not implicit authority.
Exact URI and JSON Pointer support reproducible diagnostics.
Direct, derived, defaulted, unresolved, prohibited, and missing representation are materially different.
Successful IR mappings must identify an exact frozen IR pointer.
Missing IR representation requires stable Phase 5 gap evidence.
Terminal outcomes must be explicit and machine-distinct.
Stable sorted diagnostics explain non-success without prose parsing.
Validation claims must identify the exact schemas used.
Contract validation must prove it did not access the network.
Contract validation must prove it did not read credentials.
